Black erred decisively with 39...Rd2??, and you found the clean finish. You played 40.g4+! Kh4 41.Bf2+ Rxf2 42.Rxh6#, wrapping up the game with checkmate.

review.turning_point: Black missed their chance to turn the tables after 34.Re3??, replying with 34...Kf7?? and letting you steer the game toward a mating net.
review.focus: Watch out for base-rank vulnerabilities when lifting your rooks, as on 34.Re3.

review.headline: A sharp kingside storm unseats Black's extra piece

sections.text: You punished your opponent's opening mistake 5.Be3 with the active 5...d5!, gaining space and early central control. After opposite-side castling, you pushed on the queenside with 11...a6 and 13...b5, establishing a serious initiative. However, closing the wing with 15...b4 allowed White to anchor on c4 and march the h-pawn forward.

With 16...Ne8, you created a discovered attack against the bishop on g5, but the retreat pulled defenders away from your king. White soon gifted you a full knight with 19.Na5, which you gladly snapped up with 19...Qxa5. You held a winning advantage, but White kept direct pressure along the f-file and against h7.

Under escalating kingside pressure, defending proved tricky. Grabbing the pawn with 25...Nxh6 opened the floodgates for White's queen. White replied with 26.Qh2, and after 26...Kg7, 27.Bxf7 placed a pin on your f8-rook. Recapturing with 27...Nxf7 removed the final guard from h7, walking directly into 28.Qxh7#.

review.turning_point: Capturing the poisoned pawn with 25...Nxh6 left your king hopelessly exposed to White's queen and knight battery, turning a winning game into an immediate mating attack.
review.focus: Prioritize king safety over grabbing flank pawns under pressure; on move 25...Nxh6, counterattacking in the center was vital to relieve the threat on your king.

review.headline: A sharp tactical scramble collapses against White's runaway passed pawn

sections.text: Out of the Petrov's Defense, you developed solidly until 9...Bh5?, which invited White to eliminate your bishop. White didn't punish it immediately, and the game quickly flared up in the center after 11...Nf4? 12.Bxf4 exf4, damaging your pawn structure but opening lines for your pieces.

The battle sharpened when you activated your heavy pieces. White erred with 16.Qxf4?, and after you created a pin along the file with 16...Rfe8, White slipped with 17.Rfe1?. You had a great chance to seize the advantage with 17...Nxe4, but 17...Rxe4? allowed White back into the game.

On move 18, White grabbed on d6. Instead of defending against the attack on your knight, you played 18...Qxb2??, allowing 19.Qxc5. The game simplified, but White's central d-pawn became unstoppable. After 25.d5, retreating with 25...Qd8?? let White push 26.d6 and 28.d7, completely tying you down.

review.turning_point: The critical collapse came on 25...Qd8??, which failed to challenge the advancing passed pawn and allowed White to march to d6 and d7.
review.focus: Keep your queen active and blockade passed pawns effectively rather than retreating passively, as seen on 25...Qd8.
